game.name: Slay the Spire
game.short_description: We fused card games and roguelikes together to make the best single player deckbuilder we could. Craft a unique deck, encounter bizarre creatures, discover relics of immense power, and Slay the Spire!

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Slay the Spire is the deck-building roguelike that kicked off the whole genre, and most later deck-builders descend from it. He calls it the most perfectly designed deck-builder and says it is his favorite roguelike right now, with more Steam playtime than any other game. He also thinks it is the ideal entry point to the genre because it is the simplest yet best-designed of them all. The huge modding scene adds to his love, but he says it is an S-tier masterpiece even without mods.
praise: Cards are very well balanced: none feels overpowered or useless, and each can be played several ways
Many characters with many different builds
Relics act as run-long passives that change how you play, so every run feels different
Unlocking a new card pick after the first run makes runs feel unique early on
Huge modding community adds new characters, worlds and DLC-like content; he plays almost only modded now
Simplest and best-designed deck-builder, so ideal for introducing newcomers to the genre
Lasting appeal: he has played since release and followed every update
criticism: No new official updates or DLC at this point
You cannot customize your starting deck
unique_points: It pioneered the deck-building roguelike genre and inspired nearly every game in it
Modding scene is among the biggest in roguelikes, with a recent expansion built by roughly 70 modders over years
Card and relic balance keeps variety high without any dominant or dead options
commentary.quote: this is still a masterpiece that's an S tier for me
design_criteria: Balance: no card is overpowered or useless
Build diversity: many characters and many viable builds
Synergies and run variety: relics change playstyle each run
Replayability and longevity: years of play, mod support
Visuals and audio: acknowledged as average but not important to him
Meta-progression: new card choices unlock after first run
Community and modding: huge, though he tries not to let it sway the rating

community.one_liner: A single-player roguelike deckbuilder by Mega Crit where you climb a three-act tower with one of four characters, building a fresh deck from card, relic and potion rewards each run.
community.consensus_summary: Slay the Spire is widely treated as the genre-defining roguelike deckbuilder. Critics were near-unanimous (Metacritic PC 89 from 24 reviews, all positive; a 98% critic-recommend figure is cited via Wikipedia (OpenCritic page not re-verified)) and Steam players rate it Overwhelmingly Positive at about 97.5% across roughly 219k reviews. Praise centres on tight card design, readable decisions and enormous replayability. The recurring dissent, mostly from a small negative minority on Steam, is about RNG and loss feeling undeserved. It launched in Early Access in Nov 2017 and hit 1.0 in Jan 2019, then spread to consoles and mobile. Its sequel, Slay the Spire 2, entered Early Access in March 2026 .
best_things: Card and relic synergies reward experimentation; players report discovering new builds after hundreds or thousands of hours
Highly addictive one-more-run loop: top-voted reviews show players at 150-680 hours and joking about losing sleep and study time
Four characters (Ironclad, Silent, Defect, Watcher) play very differently and each has multiple archetypes
Branching map with visible elites, shops, rest sites and events turns pathing into a clear risk-versus-reward decision that many later roguelikes copied
Enemies telegraph their intents, so combat is puzzle-like and deaths can usually be traced to a decision
Ascension levels (20 of them) plus the Heart ending give a very deep difficulty curve that keeps veterans challenged
Fast, pick-up-and-stop session format: no timers, save anytime, works offline and on handhelds, and easy to play in short bursts
Reviewers say it is accessible to people with no card-game experience while still having high depth
Strong value: frequently discounted heavily, and cited in reviews as a bargain for the hours delivered
worst_things: RNG in card rewards, relic offers and boss/elite draws can doom a run early, which is the dominant complaint in Steam negative reviews
Some bosses and encounters hard-counter certain decks; the final act and Heart fight demand specific setups that can feel like a check against the build you drew
Losses after long runs can feel undeserved or like gambling rather than skill, per several negative reviews
Characters are felt to be unevenly strong by some players, with some bosses being harsh on particular characters
Visual style is functional rather than beautiful; even positive reviews call the art plain
Console and mobile versions stopped receiving updates after Humble Games' publishing arm shut down in July 2024
No undo button, which players say makes misclicks and misreads costly
improvements: More randomness mitigation or reroll-type tools in normal runs (the Custom/constructed style modes are said to build decks that feel like cheating)
An undo or take-back option for accidental plays
Better balance between characters and against specific boss matchups
Less punishing early difficulty scaling and a gentler on-ramp to ascensions for newer players
Faster, more satisfying unlock progression, since players find unlocking cards via slow XP on each run dull
unique_things: Helped define the roguelike deckbuilder genre; its map, relic and card-reward structure was widely imitated
Enemy intent display turns each fight into a deterministic puzzle layered on top of draw randomness
Permanent meta progression is only unlocks, not stat upgrades, so every run starts equal
Deck thinning and deck-size control as a core skill: adding cards is often a mistake
A deep ascension ladder plus an optional Heart fight extend the game far beyond a first win
Has a robust mod and Workshop scene, including large fan expansions such as Downfall
tedious_or_disliked: Runs that blur together for some players; a few say the loop lacked the one-more-run pull after the first dozens of hours
Slow unlock XP that gates cards per character, which some call grindy
High win-rate grind to climb ascensions, with some players stuck near a 20% win rate and reporting frustration
Losing a long run to one bad draw or burst boss attack and having to restart from floor 1
Having to build towards the final boss while surviving the regular fights on the way up
divisive_points: RNG versus skill: fans say good play mitigates bad draws, critics say randomness overwhelms the strategy
Difficulty and ascension grind: veterans love the ceiling, newcomers find the learning curve steep
No run-to-run power progression: praised as pure skill, disliked as a lack of persistent reward by some reviewers
Endgame Heart and act 4 requirements: considered a great climax by some and an annoying build check by others
community.reception_notes: Early Access launched Nov 2017 with slow initial sales (around 2,000 copies), then took off after a large Chinese streamer featured it; it reached Steam's second best-selling slot in Jan 2018, passed 1 million copies by June 2018 and 1.5 million by March 2019. 1.0 released Jan 23, 2019, followed by PS4 (May 2019), Switch (June 2019), Xbox One (Aug 2019), iOS (June 2020) and Android (Feb 2021). It won or was nominated for multiple 2019 awards (IGN Best Strategy Game of 2019, PC Gamer Best Design 2019). Third-party estimates put Steam gross revenue near $200M and developer net near $59M (Boxleiter-style estimate, not audited), and SteamSpy-style data puts owners at 5-10 million. Steam concurrent players still around 15k per the data file. Slay the Spire 2 entered Early Access on March 5, 2026 (co-op up to 4 players, Godot engine). Console and mobile ports stopped being updated after Humble Games' publishing division shut in July 2024.
